patient.name: Arjun Mehra
patient.current_issue: Recurrent dizziness and one episode of near-syncope this week
patient.current_context_note: Presenting for evaluation after prior encounters documented dizziness after medication changes. Current med list per chart: Amlodipine 2.5 mg daily, Pantoprazole 20 mg daily.

records.title: Primary care visit — dyspepsia
records.summary: Evaluation of recurrent epigastric discomfort after meals; no alarm features.
records.body: Subjective: 32-year-old male with recurrent epigastric burning after meals, several times weekly for about 3 months. No weight loss, no dysphagia, no GI bleeding. Assessment: suspected uncomplicated dyspepsia. Medications: Started Pantoprazole 20 mg daily. Plan: trial of PPI for 4-6 weeks; return if symptoms persist. Allergies: NKDA (no known drug allergies).

records.title: Routine labs — metabolic panel
records.summary: Screening labs at annual review; within normal limits except borderline LDL.
records.body: HbA1c: 5.4%. Sodium: 139 mmol/L. Potassium: 4.1 mmol/L. Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL. LDL: 128 mg/dL. HDL: 48 mg/dL. Plan: lifestyle counseling for LDL; no medication initiated.

records.title: Prescription — antihypertensive initiated
records.summary: Home readings consistently 148/92; started on antihypertensive therapy.
records.body: Vitals: BP 148/92 mmHg, HR 76. Home log shows several readings above 145/90 over four weeks. Medications: Started Amlodipine 5 mg daily. Counseling: salt reduction, home BP log. Follow-up in 6 weeks to reassess.

records.title: Follow-up — blood pressure recheck
records.summary: BP improved on therapy; mild ankle swelling noted.
records.body: Vitals: BP 132/84 mmHg, HR 72. Patient reports mild ankle swelling by end of day. Tolerating medication otherwise. Medications: Continue Amlodipine 5 mg daily. Plan: monitor swelling; reassure if stable.

records.title: Primary care visit — persistent dyspepsia
records.summary: Dyspeptic symptoms recurring despite intermittent PPI use.
records.body: Subjective: epigastric burning has returned though less severe than 2024. Patient admits taking PPI only when symptomatic. Assessment: chronic dyspepsia, adherence issue. Medications: Continue Pantoprazole 20 mg daily, emphasize daily use. Allergies listed on intake form: NKDA. Vitals: BP 136/86 mmHg.

records.title: Medication change — antihypertensive switched
records.summary: Ankle swelling attributed to antihypertensive; switched therapy and documented a new drug allergy report.
records.body: Vitals: BP 134/82 mmHg. Ankle swelling persisted and bothers patient. Medications: Discontinued Amlodipine 5 mg daily; Started Losartan 50 mg daily. Intake note: patient reports a childhood rash with penicillin; recorded as Penicillin allergy (patient-reported, unverified). Plan: recheck BP in 4 weeks.

records.title: Labs — renal function after ARB start
records.summary: Routine safety labs after starting new antihypertensive.
records.body: Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL. Potassium: 4.4 mmol/L. HbA1c: 5.5%. Comment: values acceptable after ARB initiation; repeat in 6 months.

records.title: Specialist consultation — gastroenterology
records.summary: Ongoing dyspepsia despite daily PPI; workup planned.
records.body: History: 8 months of intermittent epigastric burning despite adherence to Pantoprazole 20 mg daily. No alarm features. Assessment: functional dyspepsia suspected; H. pylori testing ordered. Medications: Increased Pantoprazole to 40 mg daily pending workup. Allergy field in clinic intake: Penicillin (patient-reported).

records.title: Lab report — H. pylori stool antigen
records.summary: Infection testing result returned; therapy course planned.
records.body: H. pylori stool antigen: POSITIVE. Plan: eradication therapy discussed. Note: because of the documented Penicillin allergy, an amoxicillin-containing regimen was avoided; a clarithromycin-based regimen selected. Medications: Started Clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily for 14 days (part of eradication course).

records.title: Primary care visit — antibiotic course tolerance
records.summary: Patient halfway through eradication course; tolerating therapy.
records.body: Subjective: mild metallic taste, no rash, no GI bleeding. Medications: Continue Clarithromycin course (day 10 of 14). Continue Pantoprazole 40 mg daily. Vitals: BP 128/80 mmHg on Losartan 50 mg.

records.title: Hospital discharge summary — gastritis admission
records.summary: Two-day admission for severe epigastric pain; endoscopy showed gastritis; discharged on acid suppression.
records.body: Admission: 33-year-old male with severe epigastric pain, nausea. Endoscopy: antral gastritis, no ulcer, no bleeding. Discharge medications: Continue Pantoprazole 40 mg daily; Started Famotidine 20 mg as needed for breakthrough symptoms. NOTE: pharmacy reconciliation at discharge lists Penicillin V among home medications — this contradicts the documented Penicillin allergy and requires verification. Vitals at discharge: BP 126/78 mmHg on Losartan 50 mg daily.

records.title: Lab report — post-eradication confirmation
records.body: H. pylori stool antigen: NEGATIVE. Plan: step Pantoprazole back down from 40 mg to 20 mg daily over the next month. Medications: Decreased Pantoprazole to 20 mg daily (documented 2025-10-05).

records.title: Emergency visit — dizziness with near-syncope
records.summary: Acute dizziness episode three weeks after starting a new antihypertensive dose; workup unremarkable.
records.body: Chief complaint: sudden dizziness while standing, near-syncope, no chest pain, no palpitations. Vitals in ED: BP 104/64 mmHg supine, 88/58 mmHg standing. Context: antihypertensive dose had been Increased Losartan to 100 mg daily two weeks prior (per triage note). ECG: sinus rhythm, no acute changes. Glucose: 96 mg/dL. Disposition: symptoms improved with fluids; discharged with advice to rise slowly. Medications at visit: Losartan 100 mg daily, Pantoprazole 20 mg daily. Allergy band: Penicillin.

records.title: Medication change — antihypertensive adjusted after ED visit
records.summary: Dizziness reviewed; antihypertensive reduced and later switched.
records.body: Review of ED visit: orthostatic drop noted after dose increase. Medications: Discontinued Losartan 100 mg daily; Started Amlodipine 2.5 mg daily (low dose, was previously tolerated at 5 mg without severe symptoms). Plan: home BP log, return sooner if dizziness recurs. Allergies confirmed with patient: Penicillin (rash in childhood, patient-reported).

records.title: Primary care visit — symptom review
records.summary: Brief dizziness episodes persisting intermittently on new regimen.
records.body: Subjective: two brief dizziness episodes in the past week, both when standing quickly. No syncope. Vitals: BP 118/74 mmHg seated, HR 78. Medications: Continue Amlodipine 2.5 mg daily; Continue Pantoprazole 20 mg daily. Plan: symptom diary; hydration advice.

records.title: Follow-up — interval review
records.summary: Symptoms improved; plan for continued monitoring.
records.body: Subjective: dizziness much improved, one mild episode in past month. Vitals: BP 124/78 mmHg. Medications: Continue Amlodipine 2.5 mg daily, Pantoprazole 20 mg daily. Labs ordered for annual review. Note: patient mentioned filling a prescription at a new pharmacy; med list reconciliation deferred.

records.title: Annual labs — metabolic panel
records.body: HbA1c: 5.4%. Sodium: 140 mmol/L. Potassium: 4.2 mmol/L. Creatinine: 0.95 mg/dL. LDL: 122 mg/dL. Comment: stable; continue current plan.

records.title: Emergency visit — recurrent dizziness
records.summary: Second ED visit for dizziness with one near-syncopal episode at work.
records.body: Chief complaint: dizziness escalating over several days, one near-syncope at work, no chest pain. Vitals: BP 106/66 mmHg supine, 92/60 mmHg standing. Glucose: 92 mg/dL. ECG: sinus. Context: patient reports refilling prescriptions at a new pharmacy; notes a bottle labeled Amoxicillin 500 mg in his bag from a dental visit last week — flagged because the allergy band lists Penicillin. This was not reconciled with the discharge summary. Disposition: observed 4 hours, improved with fluids, follow-up recommended within one week. Medications at visit: Amlodipine 2.5 mg daily, Pantoprazole 20 mg daily.
